In a recent PR, Michael brought up that it is helpful to be able to refer to the Rocq names for ported theorems. I think this is a great idea: not only will it help with porting, but it will make comparing Iris-Lean against Iris-Rocq for completeness a lot easier.

To link the two, Michael added in a deprecated alias: 

theorem or_exists_bool [BI PROP] {P Q : PROP} :
    P ∨ Q ⊣⊢ «exists» (fun b : Bool => if b then P else Q) :=
  ⟨or_elim (exists_intro (Ψ:=λ b => if b then P else Q) true)
           (exists_intro (Ψ:=λ b => if b then P else Q) false),
   exists_elim (Bool.rec or_intro_r or_intro_l ·)⟩
@[deprecated or_exists_bool (since := "2026-01-29") ]
abbrev or_alt := @or_exists_bool -- name used by Iris Rocq

I suggest that we should make this a habit!

In a recent PR I introduced the rocq_alias attribute for this

@[rocq_alias excl_auth_frag_op_validN]
theorem frag_op_validN {a b : A} : (✓{n} (◯E a) • ◯E b) ↔ False := by
   ...

Adding a rocq_alias to your theorem or definition will add a deprecated alias to that definition under the Rocq namespace (no matter which namespace you are currently working in) to avoid Lean/Rocq naming scheme clashes. The above definition will be accessible by its Rocq name at Rocq.excl_auth_frag_op_validN. At least with my autocomplete, this means typing Rocq. will start listing out the Rocq names in the files I have imported. The deprecated aliases also support jump to definition.
(By the way, thanks to Alex for telling me this should be an attribute instead of a command!)
I noticed that the WSat commit uses rocq_alias even if the Lean definition and Rocq definition have the same name. See e.g. here Is this something we should do in general?
This also made me think if we can check the completeness of the port by comparing the rocq_alias definitions with the names of definitions / theorems / instances in Iris Rocq.

Michael Sammler said:

I noticed that the WSat commit uses rocq_alias even if the Lean definition and Rocq definition have the same name. See e.g. here Is this something we should do in general?

I think it would be a good idea, as you said that way we can use the Rocq namespace as a way to test whether a theorem has been ported or not. For a PR for #103 I'm preparing I've modified rocq_alias to accept rocq_alias ↓ so it includes the declaration's name in the Rocq namespace. My plan was to propose the change in a separate PR

rocq_alias ↓ is an interesting idea. I think it could be nice to save some typing, but I think there is also a risk that one accidentally changes the rocq alias when changing the Lean name since the two are now coupled. I guess the fancy version would be to have rocq_alias ↓ but also have a code action that replaces the ↓ with the name of the definition (and maybe a warning to not have rocq_alias ↓ in the final code?).
Fancy version number 2, we have rocq_alias check the given name against a list of all Iris Rocq lemmas, and gives an error if it's not found
I'm half joking, half wondering if it's a good idea
Not sure if it makes sense to do that in the command itself, but doing something like this in CI might actually be very nice.
Not so sure rocq_alias ↓ is a good idea either. I usually just generate the rocq_aliases and then check them, it's pretty easy and I think the AI has a 100% hit rate so far lol
The script to check for completeness could be a good idea though!
Probably also good to have if we plan to keep rocq_alias around after the port is done ("done" being a hard thing to define) for keeping up with changes to the Rocq code
Put down some ideas in a new issue. I'm tempted to steal it, since this could be a really fun coding exercise iris-lean#308

I have noticed that when adding a new, repeated rocq_alias, I won't get an error at the new definition, but at the old one, when the old one is in a file that imports the new definition. You also can't detect this by #checking the alias before adding it, since in this scenario the old definition is not available, since its file hasn't been imported.

No idea how to fix it, but I thought I'd bring it up so people are aware of this current limitation

Thanks. I'm wondering whether it's reasonable to require specifying the full access path for those definitions/lemmas in modules when using rocq_alias. This is to resolve potential name ambiguity, which I hope is good enough, given that Iris-Rocq only has light use of the module system for namespacing. For instance,
in Rocq:

Module bi.
  Lemma absorbingly_timeless P : ...
End bi.

the alias should be:

@[rocq_alias bi.absorbingly_timeless]
Whatever you think!

The script simply looks for the Module keyword, which is very ad-hoc.

Not sure if it is useful, but you can print the contents of a module using Print. E.g. the following:

Require iris.base_logic.bi.
Print iris.base_logic.bi.

results in

Module
bi
:= Struct
     Definition uPred_pure : ∀ M : ucmra, Prop → uPred M.
     Definition uPred_emp : ∀ M : ucmra, uPred M.
     Parameter pure_ne :
       ∀ (M : ucmra) (n : natSI), Proper (iff ==> dist n) uPred_pure.
     Parameter pure_intro :
       ∀ (M : ucmra) (φ : Prop) (P : uPred M),
         φ → uPred_entails P (uPred_pure φ).
     Parameter pure_elim' :
       ∀ (M : ucmra) (φ : Prop) (P : uPred M),
         (φ → uPred_entails (uPred_pure True) P)
         → uPred_entails (uPred_pure φ) P.
     Parameter uPred_bi_mixin :
       ∀ M : ucmra,
         BiMixin uPred_entails uPred_emp uPred_pure uPred_and uPred_or
           uPred_impl (@uPred_forall M) (@uPred_exist M) uPred_sep
           uPred_wand.
     Parameter uPred_bi_persistently_mixin :
       ∀ M : ucmra,
         BiPersistentlyMixin uPred_entails uPred_emp uPred_and
           (@uPred_exist M) uPred_sep uPred_persistently.
     Parameter uPred_bi_later_mixin :
       ∀ M : ucmra,
         BiLaterMixin uPred_entails uPred_pure uPred_or uPred_impl
           (@uPred_forall M) (@uPred_exist M) uPred_sep uPred_persistently
           uPred_later.
     Definition uPredI : ucmra → bi.
...
   End

I've looked into the porting status on the website for the proofmode and it seems like the name based approach for the porting there does not work so well because for the tactics there is not necessarily a 1-to-1 mapping between names in Rocq and names in Lean. Instead, it would be nice to have a bit more flexible system. I am imagining something like the following:

  1. A #rocq_ignore_file command that lets one ignore files. This would e.g. be useful for coq_tactics.v that does not map well to Lean
  2. A #rocq_concept command that lets one declare a concept in the Rocq implementation with a note whether it was ported or not. The idea would be that these would show up as a line on the website, similar to how definitions show up at the moment. E.g. one could use that to mark which tactics have been ported, something like the following
#rocq_concept iIntro ported "ported as iintro tactic"
#rocq_concept iInduction missing "to be ported"

Any thoughts on this? @Zongyuan Liu How hard do you think it would be to implement something like these two points?

Thanks for the suggestions. Implementing the two points (or similar things) would be easy.

Michael Sammler said:

  1. A #rocq_ignore_file command that lets one ignore files. This would e.g. be useful for coq_tactics.v that does not map well to Lean

I’ve considered this, but I’m unsure where to place these commands. Currently, my implementation includes a separate config file (https://github.com/lzy0505/iris-lean/blob/master/rocq_ignore.toml) containing a list of ignored Rocq files and other relevant information. If you find it natural to have them inline, I'm happy to implement it.
If we want to keep more things in Lean, we could also make the config file a Lean file in which we collect all such commands. But this would require more effort.

I agree the 1-1 name mapping is not good for proof mode tactics; that's why my script currently skips all of them. We should handle them differently.
One idea I have is that we can just use a two-level list format (similar to PORTING.md) for tactics and their features. We can either include it in the config file, or make a specialised proof-mode command so that we can inline them.
For instance

#rocq_proofmode iIntro pure_pattern ported "..."

It is slight more specialised that what you suggested. What do you think?
@Zongyuan Liu Pages is now enabled via github actions. Do you think your page ready to merge?

I’ve considered this, but I’m unsure where to place these commands. Currently, my implementation includes a separate config file (https://github.com/lzy0505/iris-lean/blob/master/rocq_ignore.toml) containing a list of ignored Rocq files and other relevant information. If you find it natural to have them inline, I'm happy to implement it.

I think it might be nicer to have it in the Lean code instead of a separate config file. In particular, it might be nice to have a Porting.lean file in the ProofMode folder that contains the #rocq_ignore_file commands (and the #rocq_concept commands). This way, the ProofMode folder is self contained and one does not need to look at other files in the repo for the porting state. Other folders that need this can also add a Porting.lean file where they put commands that explain their porting state.

Zongyuan Liu said:

For instance

#rocq_proofmode iIntro pure_pattern ported "..."

It is slight more specialised that what you suggested. What do you think?

I think it would be cool if the command does not just work for the proof mode. We might also have other places where we cannot port things 1-to-1.
I like your idea of supporting subfeatures like pure_pattern. Maybe we can simply support this by allowing dots in the name of the feature? E.g., then one can have iIntro, iIntro.pure_pattern, iIntro.modintro_pattern, ...
We probably want to give #rocq_concept a filename that it knows where it should be displayed on the website. So overall maybe something like the following?

#rocq_concept "proofmode/ltac_tactics.v" iIntro ported "..."
#rocq_concept "proofmode/ltac_tactics.v" iIntro.pure_pattern ported "..."

(A bit of a separate and minor point, but I am not sure if we actually need the "..." at the end or if we just want to use the doc string for this, same for #rocq_ignore. I.e., use the following:

/-- Ported as iintro -/
#rocq_concept "proofmode/ltac_tactics.v" iIntro ported
```)

I made a complete pass over the proofmode folder and annotated everything with rocq_alias and added rocq_concept for the missing tactics: https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/379
According to the website, the proof mode is 70% ported :tada: (In practice, I would expect that it feels like more than 70% since the missing tactics and features are less commonly used.)
In the PR, I removed the proofmode section from the PORTING.md file since I think the status website is strictly better and the duplication is annoying to deal with.
The overall porting has also just crossed 25% :tada: :tada:
